question: Do I need technical or marketing experience?
answer:
No. You do not need technical or marketing experience to use the AI Business Lab system.
The website setup, structure, design, and initial content are handled for you. You do not need to build the website, write code, manage hosting, upload products, or perform technical maintenance.
The daily actions are simple, such as activating your Daily Boost, reviewing your dashboard, and promoting your website through social media or other traffic sources.
Our Support Team can guide you through the system, and your Success Manager can explain additional packages that may handle traffic, content, SEO, social media, and other marketing activities on your behalf.

question: Do I need to upload products, articles, or other content to my website?
answer:
No. Your website is created with its initial content already included, including 30 comparison articles based on your selected niche.
You do not need to upload physical products, manage inventory, process orders, or add content manually. The website is designed as an informational digital asset where visitors can browse articles and product comparisons.
Additional articles, pages, categories, or content packages can be added later through your Success Manager if you would like to expand the website.

question: How do I know whether my website is ready and live?

Open the website domain shown in your dashboard or AI Assistant.
Check that the homepage, categories, and articles load correctly.
Make sure the link opens the public website rather than the AI Assistant or management area.

question: How does the AI Business Lab system work?
answer:
AI Business Lab helps you create and manage an online digital asset without needing technical website-building experience.
After you complete the setup process, the system creates your website using your selected niche and design. The initial website includes a domain or subdomain, logo, categories, and 30 comparison articles.
The website is designed to attract visitors through search engines, social media, referrals, online communities, or paid advertising. When visitors browse the content and interact with advertisements, this activity may generate revenue.
You can use your dashboard to access the website and monitor its activity. The AI handles much of the website’s initial structure and content setup, but traffic and earnings are not automatic and depend on the number and quality of visitors reaching the website.
Your Success Manager can also explain available options for traffic, SEO, additional content, social media, custom domains, and additional websites.

2. If your website is ALREADY live:
Open Start Here and choose “My site is already live.” Start with the Dashboard, then learn how to check Stats, add a payout method, understand Billing & Wallet, use the Free Traffic Boost, view upgrades, and use Support.

Promote your website and articles through social media, online communities, referrals, or other traffic sources
Review your dashboard and monitor website activity

question: How do I build my website?

question: What do Impressions, Clicks, Revenue, Estimated Website Value and Available Balance mean?
answer:
These numbers describe different parts of your website and they should not be confused with each other:

• Impressions — the number of views recorded during the selected period.
• Clicks — recorded clicks on advertisements or other website buttons/links.
• Revenue — the earnings calculated for the selected period.
• Estimated Website Value — an estimated value of the website as a digital asset. It is not the amount you can withdraw.
• Available Balance — money that has matured and is currently available in the wallet for withdrawal, subject to the payout rules.
• In Hold — earnings that have been recorded but have not yet matured into the available balance.

Use Stats for performance numbers and Billing & Wallet for payout/balance information.

question: How does traffic become revenue?
answer:
The basic idea is simple: traffic creates activity, and activity creates opportunities for monetization.

A simple way to think about it is:
Traffic → Views and engagement → Advertising / outbound activity → Revenue.

question: What is the difference between the Free Traffic Boost, a paid Traffic Boost, and the SEO Booster?
answer:

question: What is the Free Traffic Boost?

question: What does NET-45 mean?

All earnings generated during a particular month become eligible for withdrawal only after 45 days have passed from the final day of that month.
For example, earnings generated during January and February will become available for withdrawal on April 15, after the NET-45 clearance period for February has been completed.

The value of the digital asset: As your website develops stronger traffic, content, performance, and revenue history, its potential resale value may increase.
A simple way to understand ROI is:
ROI = Total value gained − Total amount invested
ROI can be affected by:
The amount and quality of website traffic
Visitor engagement and advertising activity
The quality and quantity of the website’s content
The niche and its market demand
The website’s domain, branding, and professional appearance
Search-engine visibility and traffic history
Boosters and promotional activity
Revenue consistency over time
The total amount invested in the website and its upgrades
The potential resale value of the digital asset
ROI is not guaranteed and may take time to develop. Each website performs differently depending on its traffic, growth, revenue, and market demand.

The amount charged
The transaction date
The merchant name shown on the statement
The last four digits of the payment method
Please do not send your full card number, security code, password, or complete banking details.

question: How can I resolve a refund dispute before it escalates to a chargeback?
answer:

The fastest option is usually to:
Contact your bank or payment provider and request that the chargeback be withdrawn or cancelled.
Ask them for confirmation that the dispute has been closed.
Send that confirmation through the **Support Center** in the sidebar so the status can be verified and the refund started. If you have not requested a refund yet, press **Request a Refund** in the "Looking for a refund?" box at the bottom of that page.
Once the chargeback has been officially cancelled, we can process the refund directly. The funds will usually appear through the original payment method within 3–7 business days, and may arrive sooner depending on the payment provider.
Our goal is always to avoid a lengthy chargeback process and return the funds to you as quickly as possible.

If those requirements are not met you may still be eligible for a 100% refund under the standard policy, but not the additional 200%. Eligibility is reviewed against the activity and records on your account.

question: What should I do if my bank flags a payment as possible fraud?
answer:

Your bank can explain why the transaction was flagged and, when appropriate, approve the payment so you can try again. Card issuers are generally the correct party to resolve fraud alerts and specific decline reasons.
Until your bank confirms that the transaction can proceed, avoid submitting the payment repeatedly. Once the restriction is removed, you can retry the purchase using the same card or use another available payment method.
Never send us your full card number, PIN, or security code.

question: What should I do if my website asks visitors to enter credit card information?
answer:

However, if a page on your own website asks visitors to enter credit card details, they should not submit any information. We will review the page immediately to confirm whether the request is legitimate and correct any technical or security issue.
Send the Support Team the exact page where this appears and, when possible, a screenshot of the message. Do not send any full card numbers, security codes, passwords, or banking details.

question: Why is my website redirecting visitors to another website?
answer:
Some links on your website, such as product links or advertisements, are designed to redirect visitors to an external merchant or advertiser website.
This redirect is part of the website’s revenue process. When visitors browse your content and click these links, the activity is tracked and may generate advertising revenue for your website. The more relevant traffic and genuine visitor engagement your website receives, the more opportunities it may have to earn.
However, if your homepage, domain, articles, or regular navigation automatically redirect visitors to an unrelated website without them clicking a product or advertisement, this is not expected.
We will review the website’s domain and redirect settings to identify and correct any technical issue. If needed, we may ask for the exact page or a screenshot showing the redirect.
